newsitem.title: USA: Sears, Roebuck share focus moves to earnings.
newsitem.headline: Sears, Roebuck share focus moves to earnings.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co shares rose Tuesday, rebounding from last week's sharp losses as investors anticipated a strong first quarter earnings report.
Sears shares fell last week after the company said it would refund millions of dollars to some credit card holders.

"My sense is that it may be that people are intelligently looking around, beginning to factor in earnings, and putting this other issue, which is largely a one-time event, behind them," said Todd Slater, retail analyst at Lazard Freres & Co.

The mean of analysts' estimates puts earnings at $0.43 a share for the nation's second largest retailer, versus $0.36 a year ago. Analysts expect Hoffman Estates, Illinois-based Sears to report earnings Thursday.

Analysts were not sure if Sears would take a reserve in the first quarter for the millions of dollars of refunds it said it would pay to some credit card holders who filed for bankruptcy. Those credit card holders still made payments to Sears under separate agreements, but Sears did not properly file all of the agreements in bankruptcy court.
Sears is also facing two class action suits over the matter, one on behalf of the credit card holders and another on behalf of shareholders.
Sears said last week it was not sure how much the issue would impact earnings.
The company's stock fell four points Thursday and Friday.
"They're going to make their (earnings) numbers and people realize Sears is a good place to put their money," Peter Schaeffer, retail analyst at Dillon, Read & Co, said.
